title: ReWeave Lifts LIBERO-PRO to 98.75% Without Updating Weights
summary: ReWeave pushes LIBERO-PRO success from 89% to 98.75% and RoboDojo from 25.5% to 58.25% by optimizing agent harness and task topology while keeping policy
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- ReWeave achieves 98.75% success on LIBERO-PRO and 58.25% on RoboDojo without updating any policy weights.
- The framework consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups, delivering 0.34× compression versus full concatenation.
- Continual learning on unseen tasks reaches 75.0% versus 41.3% for direct distillation, proving scaffold optimization works.


ReWeave, a new framework for embodied agent optimization, pushes LIBERO-PRO success rates from 89.00% to 98.75% and RoboDojo from 25.50% to 58.25% without updating a single policy weight. The method, detailed in a preprint by Yicheng Xu, Wencan Jiang, and seven co-authors on Hugging Face Papers, jointly optimizes the agent harness and an emergent physical task topology while keeping execution policies and perception frozen. Officially released on November 24, 2026, the framework demonstrates that dramatic performance gains can come from rebuilding the scaffolding around a policy rather than retraining the model itself.


## How ReWeave Works Without Weight Updates


The core innovation is explicit in the abstract: ReWeave jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction, improving success and enabling continual learning across tasks. The authors state they are keeping execution policies and perception frozen and moving only the context, workflows, and control loops around them. Failed trials get re-read against the updated topology, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width.


The framework matches verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions, consolidating 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups. That represents 0.34× the size of full concatenation, delivering substantial compression within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. The policy weights never move, yet the system extracts hidden progress and physical preconditions from interaction history.


## Benchmark Performance Across LIBERO-PRO and RoboDojo


On LIBERO-PRO, the success rate climbs from 89.00% to 98.75%. On RoboDojo, the jump is even more dramatic: from 25.50% to 58.25%. The LIBERO-PRO comparison is to the authors' own baseline rather than a leaderboard number, and the reported benchmarks are simulated rather than deployed in physical hardware. Still, the gains are substantial and consistent across both environments.


On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, a shared harness reaches 51.3%, versus 41.3% for direct distillation. Continual learning pushes that figure to 75.0%, demonstrating that the topology optimization generalizes across task boundaries. The framework proves that scaffold-level changes can unlock latent capability without retraining the underlying policy.


## Compression and Continual Learning


Specialist knowledge compression is a secondary but significant result. ReWeave consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups, achieving 0.34× the size of full concatenation. This compression happens within a compact shared harness that supports continual learning, meaning the system can adapt to new tasks without catastrophic forgetting or weight drift.


- 72 specialist units reduced to 44 reusable groups
- 0.34× compression versus full concatenation
- Continual learning enabled across unseen tasks
- 75.0% success on unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks versus 41.3% for distillation


The framework re-reads failed trials against the updated topology, extracting physical preconditions and matching them to verified local mechanisms. This iterative refinement process is what allows the system to improve without touching the policy weights.


## Context in the Embodied Agent Research Wave


ReWeave arrives in a dense week of embodied-agent papers, alongside the same-day Native LAM result on video-diffusion backbones for VLA pretraining. The timing reflects accelerating interest in systems that can learn from interaction rather than pure supervised training. While Native LAM focuses on pretraining architectures, ReWeave tackles post-training optimization through harness redesign.


The preprint is listed on Hugging Face Papers, making the full methodology accessible to researchers. The simulation-based benchmarks mean real-world validation is still pending, but the gains in both LIBERO-PRO and RoboDojo suggest the approach is robust across task structures.


## What This Means


ReWeave demonstrates that embodied agents can achieve double-digit success rate improvements without retraining, opening a path for systems that adapt through scaffolding optimization rather than weight updates. The 0.34× compression and 75.0% continual learning success on unseen tasks show that topology redesign can unlock latent capability and generalize across task boundaries. For labs building embodied systems, the framework offers a computationally cheaper alternative to full policy retraining, with gains that rival or exceed traditional fine-tuning on standard benchmarks.
